overview: This file documents U.S. State Department handling of proposed exports of explosives-related material and sporting firearms to Manchuria between 1930 and 1935. It begins with Jardine, Matheson & Co.’s inquiry about shipping nitration toluol through Dairen for the Mukden Arsenal and the Department’s explanation of the prohibition and licensing procedure governing munitions exports to China. Later papers concern Dayton, Price & Co.’s proposed shotgun shipments to a Japanese retailer in Dairen, including applications, itemized firearm schedules, correspondence, and internal memoranda debating whether Japanese-administered Dairen should be exempt from China-related licensing controls or treated as a potential conduit for arms entering Manchukuo and northern China.

subfiles.title: Jardine, Matheson inquiry about nitration toluol for the Mukden Arsenal
subfiles.about: The firm requests information and permits for shipping nitration toluol through Dairen to the Mukden Arsenal.
subfiles.summary: Jardine, Matheson & Co. proposes to ship nitration toluol to Dairen for use at the Mukden Arsenal. Believing that restrictions and a government permit apply, the firm asks the State Department to explain the requirements and provide two permit copies.

subfiles.title: State Department reply on licensing munitions exports to China
subfiles.from: Willys R. Peck, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: The Department explains the general prohibition and exception procedure for exporting arms or munitions to China.
subfiles.summary: The Department directs the firm to its June 2, 1930 press statement describing the licensing procedure for munitions exports from the United States to China. Exports are generally prohibited, but the Secretary of State may permit articles desired by the Chinese Government after notification through the Chinese Legation in Washington. The response encloses the press release and two license-application forms.

subfiles.title: Dayton, Price request concerning 35 sporting shotguns
subfiles.from: F. W. Brown, Dayton, Price & Co., Ltd.
subfiles.about: The exporter submits an application to ship 35 Stevens sporting shotguns to Sakamoto Shoten in Dairen.
subfiles.summary: Dayton, Price & Co. forwards application number 2 for the export of 35 Stevens shotguns to Sakamoto Shoten in Dairen, South Manchuria. Traffic Manager F. W. Brown asks for prompt return of the application so that the shipment can catch an early steamer.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs justification for exempting the Dairen shotgun shipment
subfiles.from: Maxwell M. Hamilton, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.to: Mr. Green, Division of Western European Affairs
subfiles.about: An internal memorandum explains why a proposed shotgun shipment to Japanese-administered Dairen should not require a license.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum argues that the shotguns will probably be used for hunting within the Kwantung Leased Territory and would not require Chinese Government assent even if destined for China. It considers Dairen an unlikely destination for military matériel such as machine guns because Japan would probably procure such arms through a major Japanese importer. Nevertheless, it recommends caution in defining general rules for arms shipments to Manchuria because of the existence of Manchukuo.

subfiles.title: Western European Affairs warning about Dairen as an arms conduit
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Green, Division of Western European Affairs
subfiles.about: The memorandum questions whether exempting Dairen from licensing could open a route for arms shipments into Manchukuo and northern China.
subfiles.summary: Green initials the proposed letter to Dayton, Price but recommends further consideration before it is sent. Although he regards its legal statements as technically correct, he warns that the proposed policy could turn Dairen into an open door for arms entering Manchukuo and northern China. He asks whether Dairen should instead be treated like Hong Kong and Macau.

subfiles.title: Departmental ruling that no license is required for Dairen shotguns
subfiles.from: Maxwell M. Hamilton, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: The Department advises that shotguns may be exported to Dairen without a license because of the territory’s Japanese administration.
subfiles.summary: The letter acknowledges Dayton, Price’s July 1 application to export shotguns to Dairen. It states that no license is required because Dairen lies in the Japanese-administered Kwantung Leased Territory. The ruling cites the 1905 treaties between Russia and Japan and between Japan and China, directing the recipient to MacMurray’s published treaty collection.

subfiles.title: Original application to export shotguns to Sakamoto Shoten
subfiles.about: The original application seeks authority to export 80 Stevens and Springfield shotguns to a Japanese retailer in Dairen for commercial resale.
subfiles.summary: Dayton, Price identifies Sakamoto Shoten of Naniwacho, Dairen, as consignee and purchaser and states that the firearms are intended for commercial resale. The attached schedule lists six lots totaling 80 twelve-gauge shotguns, comprising double-barrel and single-barrel Stevens and Springfield models. The form’s license section remains blank and contains no customs endorsements.

subfiles.title: Duplicate application to export shotguns to Sakamoto Shoten
subfiles.about: This is the duplicate copy of the application for the Dairen shipment of 80 sporting shotguns.
subfiles.summary: The duplicate repeats the consignee, purchaser, address, and commercial-resale purpose given in the original application. Its attached schedule again itemizes six lots totaling 80 Stevens and Springfield twelve-gauge shotguns with approximate weights and values. The official licensing and shipment-endorsement fields are uncompleted.

subfiles.title: Dayton, Price follow-up on pending firearms application
subfiles.from: F. W. Brown, Dayton, Price & Co., Ltd.
subfiles.about: The exporter asks whether its July 1 firearms application was received and when permission to export may be expected.
subfiles.summary: Brown reports that the firm mailed an application on July 1 for permission to export firearms to Sakamoto Shoten in Dairen. Having received no apparent response, he asks the Department to confirm receipt and indicate when authorization will arrive.

subfiles.title: Departmental reply to Dayton, Price’s follow-up
subfiles.from: Maxwell M. Hamilton, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: The Department directs the firm to its July 3 letter explaining that no export license is required.
subfiles.summary: Hamilton acknowledges the company’s July 11 inquiry concerning its shotgun-export application. He advises that the Department’s letter dated July 3 apparently crossed the firm’s follow-up in the mail. That earlier letter had ruled that the proposed shipment to Dairen did not require a license.

interest: The file is especially useful for showing how the State Department translated disputed sovereignty and treaty rights into practical export-control decisions. Its internal memoranda expose disagreement between geographic divisions: one emphasized the civilian character of sporting shotguns and Dairen’s Japanese administration, while another feared that the port could become a loophole for supplying Manchukuo and northern China. The paired original and duplicate applications also preserve unusually detailed commercial information about firearm models, quantities, weights, values, consignee, and intended resale.
